thread.title: Lanstar Voice and Data Launches Small-Business Pricing Plan for Hosted VoIP Phone Systems Serving Rome and North Georgia
thread.title_full: Lanstar Voice and Data Launches Small-Business Pricing Plan for Hosted VoIP Phone Systems Serving Rome and North Georgia

author: The Pilot News
title: Lanstar Voice and Data Launches Small-Business Pricing Plan for Hosted VoIP Phone Systems Serving Rome and North Georgia
text:
hosted VoIP phone system - Lanstar Voice and Data, LLC New tiered pricing and a limited-time local discount aim to make hosted business phone service more accessible for small companies in Rome, GA, and surrounding communities. ROME, Ga. - Lanstar Voice and Data, LLC, a hosted VoIP phone system provider serving Rome, Georgia, and the surrounding region, announced Thursday the launch of a new small-business pricing plan designed to lower the cost of entry for local companies moving away from traditional landline systems.
The new plan introduces three tiers of hosted VoIP service, each scaled to the size and call volume of small and midsize businesses, along with a limited-time introductory discount for companies based in Rome and Floyd County. The move addresses a common question among small-business owners weighing a switch to cloud-based phone service: how much a hosted VoIP system actually costs once installation, support and per-seat pricing are factored in.
"We built this plan because local business owners kept asking us the same thing — what will this actually cost us every month, with no surprises," said the owner of Lanstar Voice and Data, LLC . "We wanted an answer that was straightforward enough to explain in one sentence."
For a small business in the Rome and greater Atlanta area, a hosted VoIP phone system typically costs between $20 and $35 per user per month, depending on the features included, such as call routing, voicemail-to-email and conferencing tools. Businesses generally pay no upfront hardware investment beyond desk phones or headsets, since the system runs through existing internet service rather than on-site equipment. Lanstar's new tiered structure is designed to fall within that range while bundling setup and support at no additional charge for qualifying small businesses.
Under the new pricing structure, the entry-level tier is aimed at businesses with fewer than 10 employees and includes core calling features, an auto-attendant and standard customer support. The mid-tier plan adds call analytics, integrations with common business software and priority technical support. The top tier, geared toward businesses with more complex call-routing needs, includes advanced features such as call recording and multi-location routing.
The introductory discount applies to new small-business customers who sign up during the promotional period and are located in Rome or the surrounding Floyd County area. Lanstar said the offer reflects continued investment in serving small and family-owned businesses in the region, a customer base the company has worked with since its founding.
Local business owners have increasingly moved away from traditional copper-line phone systems in recent years, citing lower monthly costs, easier scalability and the ability to manage calls remotely. Hosted VoIP systems route calls over the internet rather than through a physical phone network, which allows businesses to add or remove phone lines without a technician visiting the site. For small businesses in Rome that operate across multiple locations or have employees working remotely, the flexibility of a cloud-hosted system has become a deciding factor when replacing aging phone infrastructure.
Lanstar's support team is based in the region and provides installation, number porting and ongoing technical support for small-business customers on the new plan. The company said bundled support — rather than charging separately for setup or troubleshooting calls — was a deliberate design choice aimed at small businesses without dedicated IT staff.
Businesses interested in the new pricing plan can request a quote directly from Lanstar Voice and Data, LLC . The company said pricing will vary based on the number of users and selected features, but the new tiers are intended to give business owners a clearer starting point when budgeting for a phone system upgrade.
About Lanstar Voice and Data, LLC
Lanstar Voice and Data, LLC provides hosted VoIP and business phone systems to small and midsize companies throughout Rome, Georgia, and the surrounding North Georgia region. The company offers cloud-based calling, installation and ongoing technical support tailored to local businesses. For more information, visit https://lanstarllc.com/
